whatItFakes: Each group-quarters type's residents are aged and sexed from a TUNABLE profile (src/core2/data/people/group-quarters.json: age bands with shares, each checked against plus or minus 0.10, and a female share with its own spread), split by largest remainder with ages spread evenly across each band. Other noninstitutional quarters start at 16: a shelter's younger children live there with a parent, which a room of residents of one sex cannot hold.
why: The research file holds each place's group-quarters count by type but no ages or sex (2020 P5); P28 has three age groups for the island areas only. Nothing in the repository holds the national age and sex profile of each type.
replacement: The 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics tables PCO3 to PCO10 (group quarters population by sex and age for each major type, national level), fetched by a researcher and read in place of the TUNABLE shares (SOURCED).

whatItFakes: Every group-quarters room record holds groupQuartersRoomMembers residents (2, TUNABLE, spread 1 to 4) of the same sex in age order, whatever its type: a dormitory double, a two-person cell, a barracks room and a nursing-home room alike.
why: No sourced occupancy per type is gathered. The number changes only how many room records exist and who is filled in together, never a count.
replacement: Each type's sourced occupancy where one exists (campus housing's rooms per resident, a prison's cells, a base's barracks), read per type.

whatItFakes: Institutions admit no one: group-quarters rooms take no newcomers and lose no one to the households' leaving rates, counted or full (src/core2/modules/counted-moves.ts skips counted rooms; src/core2/modules/moves.ts keeps full residents of rooms out of the monthly review and every booked review), so deaths and fill-ins lower each type's count and students and service members age in place year after year.
why: The moves engines move households by the ACS leaving rates, which would drift a SOURCED count of residents who arrive and leave by an institution's own calendar (a college's intake, a prison's admissions), so rooms are skipped, by the same rule for counted and full residents, and no intake is built yet.
replacement: A yearly intake through admitCountedHousehold that holds each type at its research row: a college admits a class each fall, a prison and a nursing home admit as residents leave (pool item core-group-quarters-turnover), needed before long saves.

whatItFakes: Each place's group-quarters count by type is the 2020 Census's, on April 1, 2020 (during the pandemic, college students counted at their campus housing), applied to a world that opens years later and scaled only by the world's population against the published one.
why: The Census publishes group-quarters counts by type for every place only in the decennial redistricting tables; the ACS's B26001 is the total only (Storrs, Connecticut: ACS 2020-2024 10,929 plus or minus 249, 0.954 of the 2020 count).
replacement: A later vintage of P5 when one is published, or the ACS group-quarters tables by type for places when published, read in place of the 2020 row.

whatItFakes: Counted residents of adult correctional facilities vote at the town's counted scale (src/core2/modules/voting.ts, countedScale and the counted voter loops) like any other counted adult, and may be drawn to run for a local seat (src/core2/modules/candidacy.ts, countedScreen). The state's barred share of the counted electorate still covers prisoners on average (src/core2/law-reach/group-a-voting.ts), but not concentrated in a prison town.
why: Room records are counted households to the voting and candidacy engines, which read no group-quarters type; the governing lead owns the counted electorate.
replacement: Skip counted correctional residents in the counted voter loops unless the state's law lets incarcerated people vote (incarceratedMayVote, src/core2/justice-law.ts), take the prison part out of the state's barred share, and leave them out of the counted candidacy draw; governing lead's chain (pool item gov-group-quarters-electorate).

whatItFakes: No group-quarters resident pays for their room: a college's room and board, a prison's per diem and a nursing home's rate are not billed to anyone. Residents of institutions spend nothing in town and hold no cash; college, military and other noninstitutional residents keep one person's CES nonhousing costs each.
why: The institutions have no books of their own in the world: no college, prison, base or nursing home bills its residents or is paid for them.
replacement: The institution's own books: a college bills room and board, a nursing home bills its residents or Medicaid, a prison is paid by its government, and the residents' costs move through them.

whatItFakes: Service members in military quarters have no job and no pay: they are outside the civilian labor force, so the opening gives them no civilian job and no share of the unplaced pay, and nothing pays them as service members.
why: There is no armed-forces employer in the world.
replacement: An outside armed-forces payer that pays service members in military quarters at military pay by rank and years.

whatItFakes: Only college and nursing-home rooms name the institution that houses them (the town's college directory record, its nursing-home employer); a prison's, a juvenile facility's, a base's and other institutions' rooms name none.
why: The town records no prison, juvenile facility, military base or other institution.
replacement: Prison, base and other institution records in the town, named on their rooms' dwellings.

whatItFakes: Law reach (src/core2/counted-reach.ts, src/core2/law-reach/group-b-people.ts) and the poverty count (src/core2/world-poverty.ts) read zero-income group-quarters room records as poor households: an inmate or a nursing-home resident reads as eligible and as poor. A room's counted group is keyed to the income fifth its zero or student income reads as (src/core2/modules/residents.ts, groupKeyOf); the jobs, health and births webs read no fifth for a room.
why: Room records are counted households to those readers, which read no group-quarters type.
replacement: The Census poverty universe (no institutional, military or college-dormitory residents) for the poverty count, and each program's own eligibility for law reach; laws lead (pool item laws-group-quarters-means-tests).

whatItFakes: A group-quarters room group's property-crime exposure reads as an owner's (src/core2/modules/crime.ts, a tenure other than rent reads as own), and institutional residents count in the town's exposure to violent crime like any household.
why: The crime engine reads tenure as rent or own and no group-quarters type.
replacement: The National Crime Victimization Survey's universe (households and noninstitutional residents) for exposure, with institutions' own incidents apart.

whatItFakes: Group-quarters room records are doors a campaign knocks on (src/core2/campaign-day.ts): a canvasser reaches a prison cell or a nursing-home room like a house.
why: The campaign day reads counted households as doors and reads no group-quarters type; the governing lead owns it.
replacement: Skip institutional rooms as doors (a dormitory may stay one where a campus allows canvassing); governing lead (pool item gov-group-quarters-electorate).

whatItFakes: Residents of juvenile facilities aged 5 to 17 count as the town's public-school students and seniors (src/core2/school-outcomes.ts).
why: The schools read every counted resident of school age and no group-quarters type.
replacement: The facility's own schooling, outside the town's public schools.

whatItFakes: A filled-in group-quarters resident's home is drawn as a house: a room's kind (its type) has no picture, so homePlaceFor shows a suburban house (src/bench/backdrop-places.ts), and the person card reads the room as rented with its type's name.
why: No dormitory, cell, barracks or nursing-room backdrop is admitted, and the dwelling list of src/bench/data/scene-places.json names none.
replacement: Dormitory, cell, barracks and nursing-room backdrops (asset-scene-admission) and the card's own label for a room; People v4 and the play-first lane.

whatItFakes: In a place with noninstitutional group quarters, the households' unplaced workers earn the place's median earnings (ACS B20002) blended toward the town's median recorded wage by the place's share in noninstitutional group quarters: (1 - s) times the place's figure plus s times the recorded median, s the Census count in college, military and other noninstitutional quarters over the published population (the place's figure as it is where the town records no wage). The civilian residents of its rooms are a pool apart, paid the place's figure as it is.
why: The ACS median earnings universe (people with earnings) includes residents of noninstitutional group quarters, so a college town's figure is mostly students' part-time pay (Storrs, Connecticut: $6,709 a year); paid to its renting households, it put 43.5 eviction filings in a year per 100 renter households (world seed 808522d29c84), above every state's 2018 rate but Maryland's; with the blend, and the rooms' residents paid from a pool apart, 1.3 (Connecticut's 2018 rate 3.98, Tolland County's 2.18; data/research/housing/eviction-filings-2026.json and its README). The blend is a sliding stand-in, not a measured figure.
replacement: Household residents' earnings from the ACS Public Use Microdata Sample for the place's PUMA (people not in group quarters), read in place of the blend.

whatItFakes: The jobs engine keeps full residents of institutions and military quarters out of civilian work as the counted tier does (outOfCivilianWork, src/core2/modules/jobs.ts), and staff candidates now read the same rule (src/core2/modules/staff.ts, roomOutsideLaborForce), but seating a public post (src/core2/public-payroll.ts) reads custody only: a resident of a nursing home or a barracks, full or counted, may be seated in a public post.
why: Those engines read custody from the justice engine's records (inCustody) and no group-quarters type.
replacement: Public posts read the household's group-quarters type as the jobs engine does (outsideLaborForce), once the seating of elected and appointed officials who live in such a room is ruled on, or a custody record for a correctional resident.
resolution: Staff candidates (src/core2/modules/staff.ts, roomOutsideLaborForce, full and counted) and public posts (src/core2/public-payroll.ts) read the household's group-quarters type with the jobs engine's outsideLaborForce: a resident of an institution or barracks is neither hired as staff nor seated in a public post. Found by group-quarters.test.ts in places 5007975 (a staffer) and 4037650 (a town finance director).

whatItFakes: The opening's employment target reads each county's ACS employment rate by age (employed over civilians 16 and over, B23001) over the town's residents outside institutions and military quarters, though the county's civilians include its own institutional residents: in a county with many of them (a prison county) the town's target is low by their share of each age row.
why: B23001 does not separate the institutional population. One denominator for the opening's targets and the collapse's unplaced workers (both without the residents outside the civilian labor force) keeps the opening from filling a prison's or a nursing home's share of the target from the town's households.
replacement: Each county's employed over its civilian noninstitutional population by age (ACS PUMS, or B23001 less the county's institutional residents by age from the 2020 Census DHC), read in place of the B23001 rate.
